questions.q: What relationship does a tumbling window trigger have with pipelines?
options: One-to-one — it can only reference a single pipeline
Many-to-many, just like a Schedule trigger
One-to-many — one trigger can fire many pipelines
It has no relationship to pipelines at all
questions.explain: Unlike a Schedule trigger's many-to-many relationship, a tumbling window trigger is strictly one-to-one with a single pipeline.

questions.q: What does the delay property control?
options: How long the trigger waits past a window's due time before firing, without shifting the window itself
The size of each tumbling window
How many windows run in parallel
The number of retry attempts on failure
questions.explain: delay is purely about when the trigger is evaluated relative to the window's due time — it doesn't change the window boundaries.

questions.q: What is backfill, and which trigger type supports it?
options: Automatically running every missed window from a past start time to now — supported by tumbling window triggers, not Schedule triggers
A feature only available on Schedule triggers
Deleting old trigger run history automatically
A way to skip windows that failed rather than rerun them
questions.explain: Setting a startTime in the past causes a tumbling window trigger to generate every missed window automatically, in order, honoring maxConcurrency — Schedule triggers don't support this.

options: The maximum number of windows allowed to run simultaneously, from 1 to 50
The maximum number of pipelines a trigger can reference
The number of retries before a run is marked failed
The maximum size of a single tumbling window
questions.explain: maxConcurrency caps how many ready windows fire at once — essential during backfill, when many windows might be ready simultaneously.

questions.q: How does a tumbling window trigger's run state behave compared to a Schedule trigger's?
options: It reflects the actual state of the triggered pipeline run (e.g. marked failed if the pipeline fails), unlike Schedule's "fire and forget" behavior
Both behave identically in every respect
A tumbling window trigger never reports failure
A Schedule trigger always waits for its pipeline to finish before reporting success
questions.explain: A tumbling window trigger run waits for and reflects its pipeline run's actual outcome. A Schedule trigger is marked successful as soon as the pipeline run starts, regardless of what happens afterward.
